title: Fix suggest_profit_target to use the weekly chart's channel, not the daily
description: Ch. 39 p.161 ('Stops and Profit Targets' section), read directly: 'Triple Screen calls for setting profit targets using long-term charts and stops on the charts of your intermediate timeframe... When buying a dip on a daily chart, the value zone on a weekly chart presents a good target.' This app's intermediate timeframe is daily (Wave/Screen 2) and long-term is weekly (Tide/Screen 1) -- but suggest_profit_target's channel/support-resistance target and protective_stop's SafeZone stop are both currently computed entirely off daily data. Per this explicit rule, the profit target should be drawn from the weekly chart's channel/value-zone instead; the stop staying on daily is already correct and does not change.

checklist.step: Change suggest_profit_target's channel computation to use weekly OHLCV instead of daily, per ch.39 p.161's explicit stops-vs-targets timeframe rule.
Confirm protective_stop remains on daily data (already correct per the same rule) -- no change needed there, but verify explicitly rather than assuming.
Update the existing hand-computed reference-value tests for suggest_profit_target with new expected values reflecting the weekly-based target.
Record a decisions entry noting this corrects a prior implementation now that the primary source (ch. 39 p.161) has been read directly rather than inferred.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if the response shape changes (should not -- this only changes which data feeds an existing field).

decisions.decision: suggest_profit_target's signature changed from taking already-computed `channel_upper`/`channel_lower: float | None` (previously sourced by the caller from app.signals.engine.analyse's DAILY Autoenvelope pass) to taking a `weekly_ohlcv: pd.DataFrame` parameter and computing the weekly Autoenvelope channel internally via a new private `_weekly_channel_bounds` helper (autoenvelope(weekly_ohlcv['close'], ema_period=13), default deviation_lookback=100 -- i.e. a ~100-WEEK warm-up, not 100-day). The support/resistance ('Position-style') candidate and the caller's already-detected `zones` stay daily and unchanged -- ch. 39 p.161's quoted rule is specifically about the channel/value-zone target ('the value zone on a weekly chart'), not the support/resistance technique, and app.signals.support_resistance has no weekly variant. protective_stop/stop_from_price_action (app.portfolio.risk) was verified unchanged and still daily-only, per the same rule (it is Triple Screen's intermediate-timeframe half of the stops-vs-targets split, already correct before this fix).
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected: (1) keeping the channel_upper/channel_lower float parameters and just having the caller (get_analysis in stocks.py) source them from a NEW weekly autoenvelope pass computed in the router instead -- rejected because the channel computation itself is what the checklist calls out as needing to move ('Change suggest_profit_target's channel computation'), and because this weekly channel has no other consumer to share a precompute-and-share pattern with (unlike `zones`, which IS shared with AnalysisResponse.support_resistance_zones) -- computing it fresh inside profit_target.py from a raw weekly_ohlcv input keeps the caller simpler (one fewer explicit computation in the router) and keeps the 'what feeds this candidate' logic colocated with the rest of the target-selection code. (2) Exposing ema_period/deviation_lookback as overridable kwargs on suggest_profit_target purely to make unit tests easier to hand-verify with a small window -- rejected as unnecessary production-signature bloat for a test-only need; the unit tests instead build a realistic-length (120-row) weekly fixture and cross-check the expected channel bounds via a direct call to the already-independently-hand-verified `autoenvelope()` function (see tests/unit/indicators/test_autoenvelope.py), the same 'reuse an already-verified building block as the reference value' pattern this test file already used for its protective-stop fixture (cross-referenced from test_portfolio_risk.py) before this change. (3) Deriving deviation_lookback specifically for weekly use (e.g. a shorter number since 100 weeks is ~2 years) -- rejected since nothing in docs/Analyse.md or Elder's own text calls for a different lookback just because the bar interval changed from daily to weekly, and introducing an unexplained second number would be exactly the kind of undocumented judgment call this app's decision-memory convention exists to avoid; kept autoenvelope's own existing default unchanged.
